title: Linear Issue Event Failure Rate
dataSources: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), Apple/Android screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar/todo exports.
app: Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, and calendar feeds via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=linear:issue
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(issue_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by team_name
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often Linear issue event records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each team.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize issue_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per team.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It catches which parts of your Linear issue event data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
